RAW_COLUMNS : [...RAW_COLUMNS, 'due'];\n  return columns.map");s=s.replace("function table(tickets, columns = TABLE_COLUMNS) {", "function table(tickets, columns = TABLE_COLUMNS) {\n  if (columns === TABLE_COLUMNS && tickets.some((ticket) => ticket.due !== undefined)) {\n    columns = [...columns, { title: 'DUE', value: (ticket) => minute(ticket.due) }];\n  }");s=s.replace("  const width = Math.max(...fields", "  if (ticket.due !== undefined) fields.push('due');\n  const width = Math.max(...fields");p.write_text(s)
p=Path('bin/tickets.js');s=p.read_text().replace("function openStore(file)", "function openStore(file, env)").replace("new TicketStore({ clock: systemClock, state })", "new TicketStore({ clock: systemClock, state, dueTimes: env.DUE_TIMES === 'on' })").replace("parseListQuery(options.query)", "parseListQuery(options.query, { dueTimes: store.dueTimes })").replace("command(openStore(options.data),", "command(openStore(options.data, env),");p.write_text(s)
p=Path('package.json');s=p.read_text().replace('"version": "1.5.0"','"version": "1.6.0"');p.write_text(s)
p=Path('README.md');s=p.read_text().replace('| `PORT`', '| `DUE_TIMES` | off | `on` exposes persisted due times and enables the overdue filter |\n| `DUE_HOURS_URGENT`, `DUE_HOURS_HIGH`, `DUE_HOURS_NORMAL`, `DUE_HOURS_LOW` | 4, 24, 72, 168 | positive whole response hours, at most 876000, applied only when a due time is first set |\n| `PORT`',1);s += '\nWith `DUE_TIMES=on`, command-line tickets also show `due`; raw output appends it after the existing columns.\n';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/api.md');s=p.read_text();s += '\n## Due times\n\nWhen `DUE_TIMES=on`, every ticket includes `due`, an ISO UTC timestamp set from its creation time and priority.\nIt remains fixed across priority edits and configuration changes. `GET /tickets?overdue=true` restricts the usual\ncursor listing to open and in-progress tickets with `due` strictly before now; all other filters still combine.\n`overdue=false` applies no restriction; other values return 400. With the feature off, the parameter is ignored as before.\n';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/operations.md');s=p.read_text();s += '''
## Rolling out due times

Deploy 1.6.0 with DUE_TIMES unset. At startup, the store backfills missing due times from each ticket's own creation
and priority and atomically saves them before accepting requests. New tickets also save due times while the feature
is off, but API and command-line output stay unchanged. Configure DUE_HOURS_URGENT/HIGH/NORMAL/LOW before this first
start if the defaults do not fit. The migration preserves audit history, timestamps, outbox and ticket numbers.

Check that every ticket in DATA_FILE has a due timestamp, then restart with DUE_TIMES=on. Changing the hours affects
only tickets that do not yet have a due time. Startup refuses malformed saved due values and stops if migration cannot
be saved. To hide the feature, restart with DUE_TIMES unset. To roll back further, stop the service and run release
1.4.0 on the same data file: it reads version 1, ignores the added fields and displays every ticket. An old release
rewriting the file discards fields it does not know, so back up the file before rollback; a later upgrade backfills
any missing due times again using the configured hours and the then-saved priority. Never run two writers together.
''';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('docs/decisions/0010-immutable-due-times.md');p.write_text('''# 10. Immutable ticket due times

Date: 2026-11-15
Status: Accepted

## Context

Response promises must survive priority edits, restarts and configuration changes, with staged rollout and rollback.

## Decision

The store assigns due once from creation and configurable per-priority hours. Startup backfills and saves missing
values before serving, even with the feature off. Due is optional on disk in version 1, validated when present, and
hidden in responses unless DUE_TIMES=on. Existing 1.4.0 readers ignore the additional field and can still load all tickets.
Overdue means open or in progress and strictly past due; filtering precedes pagination.

## Consequences

Operators can prepare data before exposing behavior. Old writers discard unknown fields, so rollback needs a backup
if due promises must be restored exactly after a later upgrade. Migration is data preparation, not a ticket edit, and
does not append audit or notifications or alter timestamps.
''')
p=Path('docs/decisions/README.md');s=p.read_text();s += '| 10 | [Immutable ticket due times](0010-immutable-due-times.md) | Accepted |\n';p.write_text(s)
p=Path('CHANGELOG.md');s=p.read_text().replace('# Changelog\n', '# Changelog\n\n## 1.6.0 (2026-11-15)\n\n- Persist immutable configurable response due times, backfilling existing data before serving.\n- Expose due times and active overdue filtering with DUE_TIMES=on; keep version 1 data readable by 1.4.0.\n');p.write_text(s)
